hard_fail_flags.evidence: The page presents unsupported provenance as fact: it says “Here is one real item from the October 28 agenda,” names Linden Falls and volunteer checkers, and gives meeting/item details that are absent from the client brief.
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open B/index.html, scroll to “From the agenda packet to a paragraph you can read in a minute,” and inspect the copy above the agenda/summary pair; then inspect the named city, October 28 meeting and “Checked by Dana R.” attribution. The brief names no city, agenda item or volunteer.

reason: A keeps the phone header compact and places the action ahead of a clear agenda artifact, while its sample is explicitly labelled and its interface states are more disciplined. B has a stronger editorial personality and more complete audience pathways, but its unsupported “real item” provenance and mobile navigation reduce confidence; I would reconsider if those facts were documented and the phone header were reworked.
